title: Celebrating 20 years of the World Bank Enterprise Surveys: Insights from the first complete global cycle, 2023-2026
gist: The 2023-2026 World Bank Enterprise Surveys, the first complete global cycle across 164 economies, show higher-income economies innovate more with less productivity dispersion, and that innovation correlates with employment growth and resilience to informal competition.

insights.claim: The World Bank Enterprise Surveys' 2023-2026 database spans 164 economies, and since 2006 the program has run more than 470 surveys in over 180 economies with nearly 300,000 interviews.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: The largest open comparable firm-level dataset for business-environment analysis.

insights.claim: WBES data have informed more than $90 billion in World Bank Group programs, supported over 1,300 peer-reviewed studies, and feed the Business Ready flagship report.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Shows the data's influence on development lending priorities.

insights.claim: The most productive firms are 5.9 times more productive than the least productive in low and lower-middle-income economies, versus 4.1 in upper-middle-income and 2.8 in high-income economies, consistent with resource misallocation.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Wide productivity dispersion marks markets where reallocation reforms could lift aggregate growth.

insights.claim: Only 16 percent of firms in low and lower-middle-income economies introduced a new product or process in three years, versus 23 percent in upper-middle-income and 28 percent in high-income economies.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Innovation gap tracks income level and institutions.

insights.claim: A 10 percentage point improvement in the WBES management quality index is associated with a 3 percentage point higher likelihood of innovation, rising to 4 points in more complex regulatory environments and 1 point in less demanding ones.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Management quality matters most where regulation is complex.

insights.claim: Women-led firms show stronger management practices and comparable overall performance despite operating in more challenging environments, so aggregate gender gaps can be misleading.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Raw gender gaps understate women-led firm performance once constraints are considered.

insights.claim: Innovating firms have 1.3 percent higher employment growth, with larger gains tied to fixed-asset investment (3.1 percent), quality certification (3.0 percent) and foreign technology adoption (2.9 percent).
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Capability-building activities correlate with job creation.

insights.claim: Non-innovative firms facing informal competition experience a 17 percent decline in labor productivity versus 11 percent for innovative firms, so innovation acts as a shield from informality.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Innovation moderates the productivity penalty from informal rivals.
insights.quote: Innovation can act as a shield from informal competition
